best_architecture:
Recommended: a single-agent, two-role Critique-Revise loop (Generator + Critic personas driven by the same model) structured as an explicit state machine, with optional escalation to multi-agent debate only for high-stakes or adversarial cases. This is the most defensible default for Local-Claw's self-review skill.

Why single-agent by default: When compute/tokens are held constant, single-agent self-critique matches or exceeds multi-agent debate on most reasoning tasks (Tran & Kiela 2025; 'Single-Agent vs Multi-Agent under equal thinking budgets' arXiv:2604.02460). Multi-agent debate (Du et al. 2023) typically costs ~3x the API calls (~300-400 calls/task for multi-agent Reflexion vs ~100 for single-agent) and is mostly justified by unaccounted-for extra compute, not architecture. For a local model harness where latency and token budget are scarce, the single-agent loop is the right primary path.

Core loop design (most important decisions):
1. Separate Generator and Critic ROLES, not necessarily separate models. Bind the critique to a STRUCTURED output schema (e.g., a Pydantic/JSON model with fields like {issues_found[], severity, constitutional_violations[], suggested_revision}). Structured critique fields act as targeted sub-prompts and force concrete, actionable feedback rather than vague praise (the 'Reflexion via Pydantic tool binding' pattern from LangGraph).
2. Grounded feedback signal. Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) works because reflection is conditioned on an EXTERNAL signal (test results, compiler/linter output, execution traces). For code review, ALWAYS feed the critic real signals (test runs, type checker, static analysis) instead of pure self-judgment. Self-critique without grounding hits a 'self-consistency ceiling' / Degeneration-of-Thought where the model just reaffirms its first answer.
3. Constitutional critique-revision (Bai et al. 2022) for the 'constitutional violations' requirement: supply explicit natural-language principles; the critic evaluates the draft against each principle, then a revision step rewrites. Iterate revisions (each revision empirically raises the harmlessness/quality score).
4. Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) for factual claims: draft -> plan verification questions -> answer them INDEPENDENTLY (Factored variant, to avoid the model parroting its draft) -> produce verified final. Use this specifically for fact-bearing outputs and reasoning chains.
5. Bounded iteration with a stop condition: cap reflection iterations (e.g., 2-3) and stop early when the critic returns no actionable issues. Maintain reflections in an episodic memory buffer across attempts (Reflexion's key mechanism) so retries don't repeat mistakes.
6. Escalation tier (optional, for code review of complex/critical changes): route only hard or high-risk outputs to multi-agent debate (Du et al. 2023) or an Agent-as-a-Judge panel. Cost-effective tuning: strong debaters + a cheaper/weaker judge model still performs well; the reverse does not.

Guidance — single-agent vs multi-agent for code review: Use single-agent self-critique (grounded with tests/linters) as the default for routine review; it is cheaper, lower-latency, production-mature, and has fewer failure modes. Reserve multi-agent debate for high-stakes, security-sensitive, or genuinely ambiguous changes where diverse adversarial perspectives break the self-critique ceiling — accepting ~3x cost and added coordination/failure-mode risk (Cemri et al. 2025 catalog 14 MAS failure modes). A hybrid router (single-agent first, escalate the hardest cases) gives the best accuracy/cost tradeoff.
reference_papers: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning (Shinn et al. 2023) - arxiv:2303.11366 - NeurIPS 2023. Verbal reinforcement via self-reflection traces stored in episodic memory; conditions reflection on external feedback (test/exec results). Foundational for the self-reflection loop.

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (Bai et al. 2022) - arxiv:2212.08073. Critique-and-revision loop guided by natural-language principles (a 'constitution'); RLAIF. Source pattern for constitutional-violation detection and iterative self-revision.

Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) - arxiv:2309.11495 - Findings of ACL 2024. Draft -> plan verification questions -> answer independently (Factored variant) -> verified response. For fact/claim verification.

Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate (Du et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.14325 - ICML 2024. Multiple model instances generate and critique each other over rounds; project page composable-models.github.io/llm_debate. Basis for adversarial multi-agent critique tier.

Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection (Asai et al. 2023) - arxiv:2310.11511 - ICLR 2024. Trains a model to emit reflection/critique tokens, retrieving on-demand and self-grading relevance/support/utility. Pattern for retrieval-grounded self-critique.

Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets - arxiv:2604.02460. Information-theoretic (Data Processing Inequality) and empirical argument that single-agent matches/exceeds multi-agent at fixed budget. [uncertain] - very recent preprint, exact author list not confirmed.

MAR: Multi-Agent Reflexion Improves Reasoning Abilities in LLMs - arxiv:2512.20845. Quantifies multi-agent Reflexion cost (~3x single-agent) and the self-reflection ceiling. [uncertain] - recent preprint, not independently verified.
reference_repos: noahshinn/reflexion - Official Reflexion implementation (NeurIPS 2023): decision-making, coding, reasoning tasks plus LeetcodeHardGym - https://github.com/noahshinn/reflexion
composable-models/llm_multiagent_debate - Official multi-agent debate code (Du et al. 2023, ICML 2024) - https://github.com/composable-models/llm_multiagent_debate
AkariAsai/self-rag - Official Self-RAG implementation: critic + generator training with reflection tokens, 150K training instances - https://github.com/AkariAsai/self-rag
langchain-ai/langgraph - Stateful graph framework ideal for cyclic reflect/generate loops; ships reflection, Reflexion, and LATS reference agents/tutorials - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph
NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails - Programmable guardrails with LLM self-checking for input/output safety (constitutional-style output checks) - https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails

guardrails-ai/guardrails - Validation framework for LLM outputs; structured validators and re-ask/correction loops usable as a critique-revise mechanism - https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails [uncertain] - repo path is the well-known canonical one but not re-verified in this session
key_libraries: LangGraph (Python/JS, langchain-ai/langgraph; current 0.2.x+ line as of 2026) - state-machine graphs with conditional edges; canonical way to build the generate/reflect/revise loop with bounded iteration and episodic state.
LangChain (Python/JS) - LLM/tool/structured-output plumbing; Pydantic-tool binding to force structured critique objects (Generator+Critic in one structured call).

DSPy (Python, stanfordnlp/dspy) - declarative, self-improving LM pipelines; can compile/optimize critique-revise modules and assertions/suggestions for self-refinement. [uncertain] - exact current version not verified.
Pydantic (Python, v2) - defines the structured Critique/Reflection schema (issues, severity, constitutional_violations, suggested_revision); field descriptions double as targeted critic sub-prompts.
NeMo Guardrails (Python, NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails) - async-first toolkit for self-check input/output rails; useful for the constitutional/safety-violation portion of the critique.
Guardrails AI (Python, guardrails-ai/guardrails) - output validators with automatic re-ask/correction, a lightweight critique-and-revise loop for structured outputs.

Instructor (Python, instructor-ai/instructor) - reliable structured outputs with automatic validation/retry; convenient for enforcing the critique JSON schema with self-correction. [uncertain] - included as a practical option; not surfaced directly in this session's searches.
